title: docs: the taught action:* node moves its executor keys into the `properties` bag — the spec strict face refuses flat `actionType` / `target`; land before objectui#11069 puts `objectui validate` on that face
body:
Filed by the triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post objectstack-ai/objectstack#6015, `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U`), answering the flat-vs-bag fork `5905925465` on objectui#10872 (the `pm:retriage`). ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch. Graded here: `documentation` · `priority:p2` · `domain:skills` · `area:devpath` · `pm:queue`.

## The ruling this carries: **A, the `properties` bag is the contract**

- **Governing text.** The spec's `PageComponentSchema` is `.strict()` (ADR-0089 D3a). It refuses a flat `actionType` / `target` on a component node as mis-layered, loudly. Read on objectstack `origin/main` `96e724475c`: `packages/spec/src/ui/page.test.ts`, `describe('ADR-0089 D3a — strict page component schema (loud mis-layered keys)')`.
- **Protocol first.** When the spec and what we teach disagree, what we teach moves to the spec. ⛔ Not the reverse.
- **B is not an option.** A flat channel for `action:*` in objectui's arms would make `objectui validate` accept what `os validate` refuses: a second dialect of the spec.
- **C is not an option.** Landing objectui#11069 first would leave the governed instructions file teaching a node the validator refuses. Agents copy that example.
- **No behaviour is lost.** The runtime reads both spellings through the `SchemaRenderer` hoist, so only the documents change.

## Scope

Every taught `action:*` node moves its executor keys (`actionType`, `target`, and any other executor argument) into `properties`. Read on objectui `origin/main` `3ab51503b3`; the nodes counted are `"type": "action:button|icon|group|menu"`, and the claim re-counts them:

| file | governed | action nodes | flat executor lines seen |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| `AGENTS.md` (#4) | yes | 1 | 1 |
| `skills/objectui/SKILL.md` | yes | 1 | 2 |
| `skills/objectui/guides/page-builder.md` | yes | 1 | 2 |
| `skills/objectui/rules/protocol.md` | yes | 1 | 2 |
| `content/docs/guide/quick-start.md` | no | 1 | 2 |
| `content/docs/guide/record-edit-modes.md` | no | 3 | 3 |
| `content/docs/guide/schema-rendering.md` | no | 1 | 1 |
| `content/docs/guide/layout.md` | no | 2 | 0 on a 4-line window (read in full at claim) |

- **Governed.** `AGENTS.md` and `skills/**` are governed surfaces (`node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` names them). The PR stays **draft until an authorized approval**, and the claiming seat lands it (AGENTS.md「受管面」). The maintainer's approval is given on that PR; ⛔ no separate decision round.
- **Cross-lane.** `content/docs/guide/**` is a `domain:devx` surface. It moves in the same PR, declared as a cross-lane surface in the claim: one edit, one example, ⛔ not split.
- **The pins move with the docs.** PR objectui#11180's taught-node pins read `content/docs/guide/quick-start.md`: `registered-types-validate-ratchet-10859.test.ts` and `held-public-block-arms-10872.test.ts`, both ledgered readers in `scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs`. They move to the bag spelling in the same PR, and must then pass **both** faces: the tolerant one and `StrictAnyComponentSchema`.
- **The census is a gate.** A re-grep for a flat executor key on any `action:*` example under `content/docs/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md` and `README.md` answers 0 after the change. Also run `node scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs --audit` and the root `scripts/__tests__` suite (the batch-4 lesson on objectui#10872).

## Order

- **This card lands before PR objectui#11069** (objectui#5250), which moves `objectui validate` onto the strict face. A pointer is on objectui#5250.
- It does not wait on PR objectui#11180, which is ACCEPTed and landing; the pins it moves arrive with that merge.

**Why p2.** Nothing is refused today: the tolerant face accepts the flat node. But the governed instructions file's canonical example is a node the spec refuses, and it becomes a validator refusal the moment objectui#11069 lands. It takes objectui#5250's grade, which this card gates.
